chunks: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-'Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah, from Ayyub b. Nuh, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. Musa (peace be upon them) saying:

Whoever visits the grave of my father (peace be upon him) in Tus, Allah will forgive his past and future sins. On the Day of Resurrection, a pulpit will be set up for him beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), until Allah the Exalted finishes the reckoning of His servants.

key_terms.زيارة: Visitation (ziyara) — pilgrimage to an Imam's shrine
key_terms.طوس: Tus — ancient city in Khurasan, modern-day Mashhad, burial place of Imam al-Rida
key_terms.عارفاً بحقه: Recognizing his right — acknowledging his divinely appointed Imamate
key_terms.منبر: Pulpit — raised platform for preaching; on the Day of Resurrection, a sign of elevated status

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Jawad say about visiting the grave of Imam al-Rida in Tus?
ai.summary: Imam al-Jawad (AS) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father (peace be upon him) in Tus, Allah will forgive his past and future sins. On the Day of Resurrection, a pulpit will be set up for him beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), until Allah the Exalted finishes the reckoning of His servants.' This hadith from the 9th Imam establishes the supreme reward of visiting Imam al-Rida's shrine in Tus (modern Mashhad), promising both complete forgiveness and proximity to the Prophet on the Day of Judgment.
